comparison: Perfect agreement on experimental system design (C11-C13). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the MAC system and myofilament preparation well-documented and acceptable, with no methodological concerns raised.

Disagreement on quantification adequacy for ATP-dependent reorganization (C14-C16, C19-C20). OpenEval finds sample sizes adequate (n=21 experiments, Table 1, Figures 1D, 2A-B), while peer reviewers explicitly express 'concern at the lack of quantification' and request clarification on experimental replication.

Related to quantification concerns. OpenEval finds single-molecule analysis (C29-C33) well-supported with n=152 myofilaments across 7 experiments, but peer reviewers question overall experimental quantification, which may include these claims.

Partial overlap on fragmentation mechanism (C22-C27). OpenEval notes mechanistic inferences are plausible but not directly measured. Peer reviewers question force generation interpretation more fundamentally, noting that force estimate reflects only 5-6 active heads with >80% in rigor.

Both address single-molecule observations (C34-C38). OpenEval finds evidence strong for force generation mechanism. Peer reviewers challenge the interpretation, questioning whether observed effects represent physiological force generation given the rigor conditions.

Strong disagreement on mechanistic model (C41-C49). OpenEval finds the model coherent and well-supported by established knowledge. Peer reviewers question physiological relevance, noting this is 'what is expected in traditional motility assays when ATP is kept low' and recommend tethering myosin independently.

Disagreement on computational modeling value (C50-C59). OpenEval finds simulations provide quantitative validation using established parameters. Peer reviewers question utility, stating 'It is not clear how much the simulations have helped' and requesting testable hypotheses.

Related to modeling conclusions (C70-C75). OpenEval supports conclusions about mechanism feasibility and membrane attachment role. Peer reviewers' skepticism about simulation value extends to these modeling-derived conclusions.

Strong disagreement on low ATP approach (C60-C63, C68, C83-C89). OpenEval finds the low ATP strategy well-justified by established myosin biochemistry. Peer reviewers strongly criticize this, calling conditions 'not very physiological' given millimolar cellular ATP levels versus ~3 micromolar used experimentally.

Agreement on uncertainty about in vivo relevance (C64-C69). Both identify the gap between low ATP conditions used (0.1-1 µM) and physiological millimolar concentrations. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculation; peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED and request experiments at physiological ATP.

Related concern about ATP concentration (C66-C67). OpenEval notes uncertainty about physiological applicability. Peer reviewers more strongly criticize the experimental conditions as non-physiological.

Strong disagreement on membrane attachment conclusions (C72-C75). OpenEval supports the conclusion that rigid attachment is unnecessary. Peer reviewers directly challenge this, arguing myosin-II should be tethered independently as it presumably is in cells, recommending experiments linking myosin to the minimal cortex.

Partial agreement on main findings (C76-C77, C99-C101). OpenEval finds conclusions well-supported by collective evidence. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'interesting mechanism' but express fundamental concerns about experimental conditions that temper acceptance of broader conclusions.
Related to force generation conclusions (C77). OpenEval supports the ~20 pN force estimate. Peer reviewers challenge the physiological relevance of the mechanism underlying this estimate.

Agreement on uncertainty about broader implications (C78-C80, C102). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about cytokinesis and other systems. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, challenging physiological relevance and requesting validation at physiological ATP concentrations.
Related to generalization concerns (C78). Both express reservations about extending findings beyond the specific experimental system, though peer reviewers are more critical overall.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic interpretations of dynamics (C28, C39-C40) as SUPPORTED with reasonable inferences from velocity-fluorescence correlations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific interpretational claims.
OpenEval evaluates background and motivation claims (C1-C10) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these contextual/background claims.
OpenEval evaluates literature contextualization (C17-C18, C24) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature comparison claims.

OpenEval evaluates established myosin motor properties (C81-C82, C85) as SUPPORTED background knowledge. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these foundational claims, though they reference myosin biochemistry in their critiques.

OpenEval evaluates model parameters (C90-C98) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations and justified assumptions. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate parameter choices, though their simulation utility concerns may implicitly relate.
